Homecoming
Winners!

Earlier this month, the brothers of Sigma Nu received the news that our homecoming float took 1st place at the Homecoming Parade on September 24th ! This year, we were partnered with the ladies of Sigma Alpha sorority. Our given theme was “Cowboy Fever”, so naturally we decked out the float with honkytonk-styled decor. The surface of the float was covered with saddles, hay, and other western props. Due to the diligent craftmanship of our members, two other levels were stacked on the float, ultimately making it 3 levels high! The second level was a new stained and epoxied bar with the letters ΣΝ written largely on the frontside, elevated by a small platform. The top level was a new three-sided DJ booth, also hand-crafted by our members. You can find both the new bar and DJ booth at the chapter house and in regular use. The whole project was entirely do-it-yourself and was only completed because of the collaborative mixture of every member’s time, skill, and teamwork.

Giving Day Results

This Giving Day, we raised $43,629 in 24 hours! It was the most raised by any Greek life organization by over $25,000, and the most we’ve raised in years. It is evident that the alumni network we have at Sigma Nu is by far the greatest and most involved of any fraternity or sorority on campus, and that we are continuously cared for! Thank you to all alumni who contributed during Giving Day, we wouldn’t be here at 1513 E Fraternity Row heading into 2027 without you! The funds will be awarded to us at the end of the year, be sure to check in to upcoming newsletters to see what improvements will be done around the chapter house with your generous donations.

Congrats Alumnus
Tom Lubnau!

On October 24th, Sigma Nu’s very own Tom Lubnau was formally invited to the University’s College of Law Honors Dinner. Tom was one of four people being specially recognized by the College of Law. He was awarded the Distinguished Alumni Award to honor his decades of success and achievement throughout his career, as well as his outstanding commitment, character, and leadership. He is a prime example of what it means to continue applying the values of Sigma Nu even after college. Mr. Lubnau, you are truly a role model to us all, congratulations!

Candidates vs. Brothers
Football Game

Our current Marshall, Davis Puckett arranged a team of his freshman candidates to take on the older brothers in a game of 7v7 full-contact tackle football. The younger men were fully confident that they could earn a victory over the brothers. In fact, it was the candidates who requested to play tackle football! Of course, the audacious statements and taunts from the younger members wasn’t taken lightly. In response, the brothers put up a whopping 70 points on the candidates, compared to their measly 56 points. Cowboy Rugby teammates Brayton Fitch and Lane Hamaker were putting their contact skills and physicality on display, but every Sigma Nu who played left it all on the field! The spontaneous game was a great success and example of brotherly comradery!

Brotherhood Event
at Top Golf

Chaplain Jackson Brooks hosted another outstanding brotherhood event, this time at Top Golf in Thornton, Colorado. Jackson rented five bays for two hours, and the chapter made the 120 mile pilgrimage in a caravan of 8 cars. The men of Sigma Nu had great competition with each other, ate delicious food, and enjoyed every minute of the short road trip. Thank you Chaplain Brooks for yet another successful and memorable brotherhood event!

Congrats New
Candidates!

On Sunday, October 4th, our pledges underwent one of the primary rituals of their pledgeship semester. After a month, they were officially made candidates of Sigma Nu. This ritual makes them one step closer to becoming a true knight of the Legion of Honor, which will occur at the beginning of next semester if they complete all necessary requirements. Every member who accepted their bid from Rush Week in early September made it to their candidate ceremony a month later!
